name: Gluten Free BITTE (グルテンフリーBITTE)
why: Describes itself as 「コンタミネーションを徹底管理した小麦不使用・完全グルテンフリーのお店」; 小麦 unticked on all 24 catalogued products; gluten-intolerant owner-baker. Also filed under Nagoya but located in 尾張旭市, and since April 2026 opens once a month by reservation.

name: laccola (ラッコラ)
why: The high->options downgrade rested on "the shop makes no blanket GF claim". laccola.com's own header and meta description do make one, and every storefront item is 米粉-based with no 小麦 in any 原材料. Keep the uncertified-oat caveat, whose real evidence is laccola.base.shop rather than the komeko-palette page cited.

name: しかさんしょこら（Shika san chocolat） (Shika san chocolat)
why: Single-product shop excluding 小麦粉, 米粉 and baking powder outright, corroborated by two sources, yet sits at options.

name: めん馬鹿一代 (Menbaka Ichidai (Menbaka Fire Ramen))
why: The 2026-07-02 downgrade cites a "shared boiling water" line the owner has publicly retracted as outdated menu phrasing. Across 38 FMGF reviews: a dedicated separate pot, symptomatic celiacs reporting no reaction, and the two "not safe" reviews are from people who read the stale line and left without eating.

name: Big Mountain Cafe＆Farm（ビッグマウンテン カフェ＆ファーム） (Big Mountain Cafe & Farm)
why: Cut high->options largely on a HappyCow line no agent can reach (Incapsula blocks every UA, proxy and Wayback). Every reachable source contradicts it: FMGF titles it "Dedicated Gluten-Free Restaurant in Nara" with 20 dedicated-fryer reports, 24 "Dedicated GF" tags, zero symptom reports and a review six days old; Tabelog publishes a 28-allergen pre-booking protocol naming 小麦. safety.dedicated_fryer is still null on the record.

name: Aimo (あいも)
why: The dedicated->options downgrade rests on an allergy-LIABILITY disclaimer rather than any wheat on the premises. The cited guide, updated 2026-07-26, lists it among 90 shops where 「工房・店内に小麦粉を一切持ち込まず」.

name: 浅草 更科天狐（さらしな てんこ） (Asakusa Sarashina Tenko)
why: Found independently by two agents on two different passes. The record is twice told "no source confirms a dedicated fryer / cross-contamination handling" while its OWN cited FMGF page carries 7 dedicated-GF-fryer reports plus dedicated-kitchen and glove-change reports. Separately, the menu pass read the shop's own 14-allergen PDF: 小麦 and 大麦 are clear on the noodles, tsuyu, tempura, karaage and yakitori tare. Two printed exceptions must survive any promotion — やま幸鮪の手巻き is marked 「グルテンが入っています」, and 蕎麦前盛り合わせ carries 大麦 via 山ウニ and is built into all three courses.

name: 杏もん堂 (Almondou)
why: Rated 'Not gluten-free' while the shop's own site states the curry uses no wheat flour and passed a third-party gluten/gliadin test with NONE DETECTED, the report displayed in store. The record also has 18 spices for 21, calls almond-milk lattes dairy, says allergy language does not exist when it does, and publishes stale hours.

name: Gluten-Free Deli AL CAMINO
why: UNDER-RATED, and this is the BITTE pattern almost exactly. The record shows 'GF - ask' on a venue whose own name is Gluten-Free Deli, whose own site says 「グルテンフリー専門店」, whose operator-written Tabelog corporate listing carries the headline badge 'Gluten Free Specialty Store' plus 'We accommodate various allergies' and 'Allergy information available', and whose FindMeGlutenFree listing reads 'Reported to be dedicated gluten-free' across 11 recent ratings - nine of them tagged 'Dedicated GF', with two 'Dedicated gluten-free kitchen' safety reports and a celiac review five days old saying 'The menu is totally gluten free'. The shop went gluten-free because the owner became gluten-intolerant. Even the beer is 小麦・大麦不使用. Two things the human gate should weigh before promoting: (a) one recent celiac reviewer logged 'Yes - mild symptoms' while still marking the kitchen dedicated, and (b) the same owner runs a wheat PANINOTECA, two wheat Italian restaurants and a frozen-pizza business under the il Viale group, though AL CAMINO trades from a separate address. If those give pause, 'high' (Strong GF focus) is the floor - 'ask' is not defensible either way.

name: Hachidori Table
why: UNDER-RATED. The record carries 'GF - ask' (GF unverified) while the operator states on its own Tabelog corporate listing 「Some menu items are available as 'gluten-free.'」 and Vegewel lists the shop with a 「グルテンフリーメニューあり」 badge in both languages. Documented gluten-free items are exactly what 'Some GF options' means; 'unverified' is inaccurate. The cross-contact warning stays in the detail text unchanged - Sesame Ramen, Soy Meat Katsu Don and curry udon share the kitchen and nothing describes a dedicated station - so this promotion adds information without lowering anyone's guard.

name: 焼鳥 あらい (Yakitori Arai)
why: UNDER-RATED. 'no' says a vegan cannot eat here, but the shop's own 公式 menu (67 items, 更新日 2026/03/28) carries a headed 野菜串 section — 白ネギ, ししとう, にんにく, しいたけ — plus 枝豆, トマトスライス, きゅうり一本漬け, 辛味噌キャベツ and なめたけおろし, and prints 「塩・タレからお選びください」 so the tare can be declined in writing. The record's own menus file already marks 枝豆 vegan and the three vegetable skewers vegan:ask, so the label contradicts the record's own data. The real caveats — shared binchotan grill, chicken drippings, likely bonito on the 冷奴 — are exactly what 'ask' is for.

name: Bistro Beppinsha (カリー＆ワイン ビストロべっぴん舎 お茶の水本店)
why: The operator's masthead is 「Gluten Free Spice Curry」 and it states 「小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーカリー」 / 「The spice curry without wheat flour」, corroborated independently by rurubu's own tasting note 「小麦粉を使っていないのでスープのようにさらさら」. The live menu is four curries and beer — there is no bread, naan, roux or fried side for a GF item to be an 'option' among — and dinner, course and à-la-carte service are currently suspended, so the shared-bistro-sides risk the record cites is not being run. A wheat-free-by-design core menu declared by the operator and corroborated by a third party is 'options', not 'ask'. Hold at 'options' and no higher: the seasoning (soy/Worcester) is undisclosed and there is no allergy protocol, so the 'confirm the seasoning' hedge must stay in gf_detail.

name: 神山（旧店名：清山） (Kamiyama)
why: The record downgrades to a flat 'Not gluten-free' on the explicit ground that 'there is no confirmation the noodles are consistently 十割 rather than the common 二八 blend' — but the operator's own HotPepper page says exactly that: 「十割で季節により厳選された蕎麦。塩でもお召し上がり頂けます。」 100% buckwheat, and a salt service that removes the wheat-soy tsuyu from the plate. This is a recommendation to 'ask', NOT above it: 打ち粉 dusting flour is unresolved, tempura is on the menu, and there is no allergen protocol — 十割 alone is never celiac-safe. But 'no' is telling a celiac not to bother asking about the one dish here they might actually be able to eat.

name: Sumatra Curry Kyoeido (スマトラカレー 共栄堂)
why: The record's own gf_detail already concludes 'it caps at options, not high' while gf_confidence carries 'ask' — the label contradicts its own detail text. The evidence supports 'options': the operator states in its own words that the curry sauce uses 小麦粉を一切使わず, the rice is plain Koshihikari, and both facts are independently corroborated by kanda-curry and san-tatsu. CONDITIONAL, and the condition is not optional: do not promote until gf_detail is corrected to exclude タンカレー and ハヤシライス, which the operator and san-tatsu both say are built on house-made デミグラスソース (a wheat-roux sauce). The record currently tells celiacs to 'Order any curry over plain Koshihikari rice'; under that wording a promotion would make the advice more dangerous, not less.

name: 肉汁水餃子 餃包 新宿店 (Nikujiru Suigyoza Gyopao Shinjuku-ten (Juicy)
why: The record treats the GF story as one marketing blog post, but the shop's operator-maintained Gurunavi menu labels roughly fifteen dishes 【グルテンフリー】 in a deliberate two-tier scheme that also marks 【グルテンフリー・ベジタリアン】 — 鶏肉チマキ, よだれ鶏, 蒸し鶏のネギソース, クラゲきゅうり, 麻辣ピーナッツ, 青菜の塩ナムル, 自家製極太メンマ, 胡麻ダレ冷やしトマト, パクチーだけのサラダ and more, most of them cold or steamed and never near the fryer. That is precisely the protocol definition of options: named adaptable dishes with no special handling. It cannot go above options — every source is the operator's own voice, which the HARD RULE caps — and the options text must carry two warnings the evidence now supports outright: the kitchen is a wheat water-dumpling line, and the shop deep-fries wheat gyoza and wheat spring rolls in the same oil as its own GF-labelled 油淋鶏, so that one labelled dish should be avoided. Left at ask, a celiac in Shinjuku is told nothing about fifteen dishes the operator has already labelled for them.

name: 新宿ダイアログ (Shinjuku Dialogue)
why: This is the honest upgrade this record has been denied. The Wednesday operator states in its own Vegewel listing 「当店はシェアカフェ新宿ダイアログで水曜日の11:00-17:00のみ営業しているヴィーガンのお店です」 — an entirely vegan kitchen on a known day and time, not a maybe. Time Out (2026-05-01) independently records that Saturday and Sunday lunchtime is 「体に優しい手作りスイーツやビーガンメニューを楽しめるカフェ」, and the venue's own Facebook bio advertises 「ヴィーガンのホームメイドケーキ」 for 毎週土・日12:00-17:00. Both Vegewel listings for the address carry ビーガンメニューあり. Three named, dated, day-specific vegan services is 'Some vegan options', not 'Vegan — ask'. It should NOT go higher: the same sources show 百福's meat-and-fish course on 月火水金 evenings and Vegewel notes 「バーのフードメニューはプラントベース料理以外も取り扱っている」, and the Wednesday operator itself warns 「他の曜日はヴィーガンではない他店様が営業しています」 — so vegan_detail must keep the day-of-week caveat prominently.

name: 築地本願寺キッチン
why: This is a DOWNWARD correction of a displayed label, not of the stored tier. The stored vegan_status 'ask' is defensible, but vegan_label 'Fully vegan' and category 'VEGAN' are what the app actually shows, and they are contradicted by the venue's signature dish: six confirmed animal items in the 18-dish set (湯葉いくら, 海苔明太, タコの塩麴和え, 築地紀文のお魚とうふおぼろ揚, 合鴨の山椒焼き, ちりめん) plus 卵焼き. Set vegan_status 'limited', rewrite vegan_label to match, and move the record out of category VEGAN.

name: べっぴん舎
why: UNDER-RATED. The record carries gf_uncited_downgrade {from: 'options', date: 2026-08-20, 'Tier held down: no safety finding on this record cites a source. Restore through REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md once evidence is attached.'} — that condition is now met. The operator's own site states 「小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーカリー」 and 「The spice curry without wheat flour」, and the Kanda Curry Grand Prix organiser states the same thing independently of the shop. Every curry on the published menu is wheat-flour-free and no naan or bread appears anywhere on it. Restore 'options'. Do NOT act on the record's separate gf_proposed_tier of 'high': there is no dedicated-equipment claim, no allergen protocol, no certification, and the shop still braises in wine and shares one small lunch-only kitchen — 'options' is what the evidence carries. Fix the Jimbocho pin first; a restored GF tier pointing at a branch that closed in 2023 would send a celiac to the wrong door.

name: アトミヨソワカ 蔵前店
why: UNDER-RATED, and the record already knows it — it carries gf_uncited_downgrade {from: 'options'} whose stated condition ('restore once evidence is attached') is now met, alongside a gf_proposed_tier of 'dedicated'. The evidence: the brand's own identity line is 「ヴィーガンスイーツ・グルテンフリースイーツ 米粉菓子」, it states 「米粉を使っているので、小麦アレルギーの方も安心してお召し上がりいただけるおいしい米粉菓子です」, and all 24 published products are rice-flour bakes with no wheat item anywhere on the site. Per the owner's ruling, writing 小麦アレルギー rather than セリアック does not weaken this. 'high' rather than 'dedicated': the operator never states a dedicated facility or equipment separation, uses organic oatmeal of unstated gluten-purity, and co-produces part of the range at an external workshop (ろくえもん) whose handling is undocumented. Those two questions are exactly what REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md's human gate should put to the shop before anything above 'ask' goes live.

name: 味農家
why: UNDER-rated for the same reasons as tokyo3__174: one gluten-free course by design, no second non-GF course to share the kitchen with, reservation-only with nothing pre-batched, one chef, advance dietary requests accepted in writing. Ceiling is 'options' and no higher, because the operator states the gluten-free is a culinary choice — 「アレルギー対応としてではなく」 — and never names the shoyu or miso.

name: 味農家
why: Recorded as a NEGATIVE result, now urgent. During this sweep a sibling process moved this record from vegan_status 'full' to 'options'. That is correct for four of the five 'Fully vegan' records in this shard but WRONG here: the operator states 「肉・魚・卵を一切使わない本格和食のコース」 and 「出汁は昆布と野菜のみで丁寧に取り、動物性のものは使用しておりません」, and the English site says 'All courses are vegan-friendly and gluten-free.' Worse, its duplicate tokyo3__174 was left at 'full', so one restaurant now shows two different vegan tiers in the app.

name: グルテンフリー ティーズキッチン 上野広小路店
why: THE MOST SEVERE UNDER-RATING IN THIS SHARD. A celiac searching this app is currently told to 'ask' at a restaurant that is named 'Gluten Free T's Kitchen', holds third-party certification from The Gluten Intolerance Group — 「アジア初のグルテンフリー認証」 — serves 「小麦・大麦・ライ麦を使わない料理や飲み物」 across the whole menu with no wheat item anywhere on the board, and discloses its only residual risk (supplier facilities that also handle wheat) unprompted. That is the textbook definition of 'dedicated'. The gf_uncited_downgrade note says 'Restore through REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md once evidence is attached' — this sweep attaches it: /about-us/ names the certifier verbatim, and /menu/ carries the wheat-free statement and the limited-space allergy caveat.

name: 玄米菜食
why: The venue's own site publishes a named 「グルテンフリー・五葷抜き / Gluten-Free」 menu section with six priced items, in Japanese, English and Chinese. Under REVIEW_PROTOCOL that is 'some naturally-GF/adaptable dishes, NO special handling' — options, and capped there because it is a single source with no independent corroboration and no dedicated fryer claimed. The mandatory cross-contamination text must say: the same kitchen deep-fries wheat spring rolls and tempura, one GF-line item (揚げ餅) is itself deep-fried, the mock-meat karaage is seitan (the venue's own English menu calls it 'gluten chicken'), and neither tamari nor the miso type is stated.

name: lei 小麦を使わない国産ビストロ 秋葉原
why: UNDER-RATED. The record was cut to "ask" on 2026-08-20 solely because no finding cited a source (gf_uncited_downgrade from "options"); the sources exist and are unusually good for a Tokyo venue. The Tabelog listing is marked 公式 — owner-maintained — and reads 「小麦・添加物・化学調味料不使用の料理をご提供しています」 with こだわり 「【国産食材・無添加・無化調・小麦不使用】」; the manager is quoted by the Kanda Curry Grand Prix organisers saying 「グルテンフリーのビストロカレー … 小麦粉不使用」; the bread is 「小麦粉は一切使用せず」; and a gluten-free/wheat-allergy blogger visited and wrote 「シェフが小麦アレルギーとのことで相談もできて安心♫」. The shop opened 2025-01-06 and is trading now (reviews 2026-06, a social post four days ago). Restoring "options" is the minimum the evidence carries, and a human reviewer could reasonably argue "high" at the REVIEW_PROTOCOL gate. But the record's pending gf_proposed_tier of "dedicated" should be REFUSED, for three reasons no source rebuts: (1) every statement is 小麦/小麦粉 — wheat — and none of them says gluten-free as to barley, rye or oats; (2) the shop pours barley beer, listing 「限定プレミアムビール」 among its three headline こだわり, and both a Tabelog reviewer (「ガージェリーという都内でも4店舗ほでしか取り扱っていないビールがありました」) and Gargery's own stockist page put ガージェリー in this room; (3) no soy sauce or tamari brand is named and no cross-contamination protocol is published anywhere.

name: Oh Nana!
why: UNDER-RATED, and the record already knows it: gf_proposed_tier reads to "dedicated", held at "ask" by gf_uncited_downgrade purely because nothing cited a source. The sources now exist. The venue is a 100% gluten-free restaurant founded by a diagnosed celiac and describes itself as 「日本初欧米基準のセリアック病対応ができる完全グルテンフリーレストラン」; an independent, explicitly unpaid visit by glutenfreejapan.jp (2026-08-05) reports 「食事はすべて厳格なグルテンフリーのキッチンで調理しています」 and 「使用している原材料や調味料はすべてグルテンフリーです」; veggy.jp independently headlines it 「100％グルテンフリーレストラン」. Recommend only — this needs REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md pass 3 and human sign-off, because a dedicated badge is exactly the label that stops a celiac checking.

name: Osteria Lauro
why: UNDER-RATED by one notch, and only for a paperwork reason: gf_uncited_downgrade records that this record was held down from "options" on 2026-08-20 solely because no safety finding cited a source. Sources now exist and are unambiguous — a named, priced, weekly-rotating rice-flour (米粉) gluten-free fettuccine at lunch, a documented +150 yen dinner substitution stated in Japanese and English, the bread deliberately omitted from the GF set, and Tabelog carrying 「グルテンフリーメニューあり」 as a venue attribute. That is 'options', not 'unknown'. It must NOT go above options: nothing published addresses shared pasta water, and that gap is the whole risk.

name: RICE HACK グルテンフリーベーカリー
why: UNDER-RATED, and the record already knows it: gf_proposed_tier reads to "dedicated", held at "ask" by gf_uncited_downgrade only because nothing cited a source. The sources exist. FindMeGlutenFree titles the listing 「Dedicated Gluten-Free Bakery in Shibuya City」 with 「Reported to be dedicated gluten-free」 over 122 recent ratings, and two independent celiac reviewers — one self-described Symptomatic Celiac — filed it Dedicated GF with 「No symptoms」 within the last month. The operator is a wholly rice-flour business (米粉使用グルテンフリー料理のカフェ、パン屋、料理教室) whose pizza it calls 完全グルテンフリー. Recommend only; a dedicated badge needs REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md pass 3 and human sign-off.

name: グルテンフリー T's Kitchen 上野広小路店
why: This record's own gf_detail opens "This is one of the safest GF options in Tokyo for a celiac" while the label reads 'ask' — the label contradicts its own detail text, in the direction that costs a celiac a genuinely safe meal. The venue states 「小麦・大麦・ライ麦を使わない料理や飲み物を提供しています」, is certified by The Gluten Intolerance Group (「The gluten intolerance group からアジア初のグルテンフリー認証を受けた」, GFCO programme), wraps its gyoza and batters its karaage in rice flour, and has no wheat batter on site for the shared fryer to carry. The only residual risks are supplier-level (「材料によっては同じ工場内で小麦を取り扱っている」) and a no-guarantee note that is explicitly about NON-gluten allergies. If 'dedicated' is reserved in this app for venues with zero acknowledged supplier-level cross-contact, then 'high' is the correct floor — but 'ask' is indefensible here.

name: そらのいろ ニッポン
why: The record's gf_detail states in terms that it is 「[Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is.」 It is now traceable, on the shop's own pages: a グルテンフリー塩ラーメン 「食材から小麦をすべて取り除いた」 on brown-rice noodles from 宮内舎 in Shimane; staff who proactively ask every customer 「小麦アレルギーの有り無しをお伺い致します」; a separate boiling kettle 「茹で釜を別にて対応させていただきます」; wheat removed from tare, oil and toppings; and the founder stating he developed it so 小麦アレルギーやセリアック病 customers could eat. That is a documented GF menu item with a named protocol — 'options', not 'ask'. It should NOT go higher: the shop itself prints 「※コンタミネーションの可能性はございます」 on that very bowl and the counter boils 全粒粉入り wheat noodles alongside.

name: 藤い屋 宮島本店 (Fujiiya Miyajima Honten)
why: Fujiiya publishes a complete 原材料 list and an explicit アレルギー line for every product, and at least two of its lines declare no wheat at all — 花虎白 is 「原材料：砂糖、フランボワーズ／マンゴ／西洋梨、寒天」 with 「アレルギー：不使用」, and 淡雪花 declares 「アレルギー：ゼラチン」 only. A blanket 'no' tells a celiac there is nothing here, which the maker's own labelling contradicts. 'ask' is the honest tier: real wheat-free items exist and are labelled, but Fujiiya publishes no cross-contamination or segregation statement and the main line is wheat castella, so a celiac must still confirm handling in store.

name: 藤い屋 宮島本店 (Fujiiya Miyajima Honten)
why: 花虎白 is sugar, fruit purée and 寒天 (agar, seaweed) with 「アレルギー：不使用」 — plant-only, per the maker's own declaration, and named on the record's cited page as part of the Miyajima lineup. Everything else is animal-containing and should stay flagged: momiji manju is 卵・小麦 castella, 淡雪花 is set with ゼラチン, and 杓子せんべい and the sablés carry egg, butter and dairy. One documented plant-only item in an otherwise animal-heavy range is 'limited', not 'no'.

name: ぎゃらりぃ宮郷 (Gallery Miyazato)
why: The operator's own current menu states the パキスタンカレー is chicken and vegetables simmered in olive oil with spices, 「水は使わず味付けは塩のみ」 — salt only, so no soy sauce and no wheat roux — served with rice and a carrot salad, and the blog photo confirms it arrives on turmeric rice with a キャロットラペ. ぜんざい (azuki with grilled mochi), 白玉冷やしぜんざい, お抹茶単品 and 甘酒 are likewise wheat-free by composition. 'no' with the detail text saying 'at most a plain coffee or tea' denies a celiac a documented flour-free main dish; 'ask' is honest because the same small kitchen bakes chiffon cake daily and toasts bread, so cross-contact is real and unprotocolled.

name: 広島大衆居酒屋 十升 流川通り店 (Hiroshima Taishu Izakaya Tomasu Nagarekawa-d)
why: The shop's own printed menu carries several plant-only dishes — 銀杏の塩炒り (ginkgo and salt), 茹で枝豆, トマトスライス, やみつききゅうり, セロリの浅漬け, らっきょう, ポテトフライ — and this record's own menu_verified entry already flags 16 items vegan, so a flat 'no' contradicts the record's own data. 'limited' rather than 'options' because only three or four are certain (the asazuke and pickle brines commonly carry dashi or soy and would need a staff check), and nothing on the menu is labelled vegan by the shop.

name: 貝や 廉 (Kaiya Ren)
why: The record's own cited Gnavi page lists 「ベジタリアンメニューご相談」 (vegetarian menu on consultation) under メニューのサービス, which is a documented accommodation, not an absence — the same class of self-reported evidence this sweep accepted as 'supported' for Itsukushima BARL Issai, which carries 'ask'. The kitchen is genuinely all-shellfish and 貝出汁 runs through it, so nothing above 'ask' is warranted, but a flat 'no' contradicts the shop's own listing and should be reviewed.

name: 牡蠣屋 (Kakiya)
why: The venue's own menu page says 「No fish. No meat. Just Oysters」 and lists only five food items, two of which are naturally gluten-free as served: 焼き牟蠿 (oysters seared in the shell over open flame, no batter and no sauce) and 生牟蠿 (raw, Nov-Mar). Only 牟蠿フライ uses the fryer, and the wheat risks (佃煎, 味噌汁, the oyster-sauce oil-preserve) sit in separate dishes rather than in the grill line. "Not gluten-free" tells a celiac to skip a shop whose signature item is a bare grilled oyster; "ask" is the accurate call — it still requires the diner to confirm the grill and the set-meal sides themselves. No allergen policy is published, so nothing above ask is defensible.

name: 牡蠣祝 (Kakiwai)
why: The current official menu has exactly four food items: 広島レモンレアチーズケーキ, チョコレートケーキ, 牟蠿屋のオイル漬け ¥1,500 and 生ハムの盛り合わせ ¥1,850. The last two carry no batter, no noodle and no cooking step — the oil-preserve arrives as a jarred product from the affiliated 牟蠿屋 and the ham is sliced — so the record's "cannot be assured anything is safe" overstates a cake-and-drinks cafe where half the food menu is plated cold. The oil-preserve is made with オイスターソース, which is commonly wheat-thickened, and no allergen information is published, so "ask" — not anything higher — is what the evidence carries.

name: 寿屋珈琲 幟町店 (Kotobukiya Coffee Noboricho)
why: The operator's own page documents 「約30種のコーヒー豆」 sold by hand-drip — 「ハンドドリップメニューは、新鮮な豆をその場で挽き、ハンドドリップで丁寧においれします。約30種のコーヒー豆からお好きな豆をお選びいただけます。」 — so a plant-based visitor has a real, documented, dairy-free order at a coffee specialist, not merely a theoretical one. 'no' also contradicts the record's own positives line, which already says black coffee here is naturally plant-based. 'limited' rather than 'options' because it is drinks only: the same page markets 珈琲ソフト (soft serve), 珈琲ゼリーソフト, バタートースト and 専用のマシーンで焼くオリジナルパニーニ, and no plant milk is advertised anywhere on the site.

name: お好み焼まとちゃん (Okonomiyaki Matochan)
why: The shop's own menu labels ポテサラチーズ焼 as 「ベジタリアン可」 with the note 「肉・魚が含まれませんのでベジタリアンの方にもお食事頂けます」, and lists four self-made tofu dishes including a mozzarella-free 豆富のカプレーゼ served cold. That is an operator who already thinks about excluding meat and fish, so a vegan has something concrete to ask about; 'no' tells a reader not to bother. Still not 'options' — every flagged item contains cheese or egg and nothing is stated to be vegan.

name: やまだ屋 宮島本店 (Yamadaya Miyajima Honten)
why: ask — the record's 'Not gluten-free' rests on the assertion that both signature products are wheat-flour cakes, and that is wrong for one of them. The operator's statutory allergen table gives 桐葉菓(とうようか) as もち粉-based with 「特定原材料 乳、卵」 and no 小麦, the same for the entire 餅 series, and 富久者有智 carries no 特定原材料 at all. Wheat labelling is legally mandatory in Japan, so these are declared wheat-free products, not guesses. No segregation or cross-contact control is documented anywhere on the site and the momiji-manju batter is wheat, so nothing above 'ask' is defensible — but 'no' tells a celiac on Miyajima there is nothing here, and the operator's own label says otherwise.

name: やまだ屋 宮島本店 (Yamadaya Miyajima Honten)
why: limited — 富久者有智(ふくわうち) is 「砂糖（国内製造）、小豆、きな粉（大豆）、水飴／着色料（紅麹、クチナシ）」, an entirely plant-based own-brand 和菓子 sold under やまだ屋銘菓, with 「アレルギー物質（特定原材料） -」. Exactly one item out of roughly 45 and the shop makes no vegan claim, so 'limited' rather than 'options'; but 'no' is contradicted by the operator's own ingredient line. Everything else carries 卵 and/or 乳 (ふわもち桜 adds はちみつ), and /tenpo/ warns 「店舗によってお取扱い商品が異なる場合がございます」, so the detail text should name the one item and say stock varies by store.

name: 甘納豆かわむら (Amanatto Kawamura)
why: options — the maker prints a full 原材料 line for every retail item and not one contains wheat: 22 of the amanatto are 「豆、砂糖、有機砂糖／甘味料（トレハロース）、還元水飴」, the rest are 栗/芋/クルミ/ピーカン/カシューナッツ/柚子/伊予柑/ブラッドオレンジ/オリーブ plus sugar, and the philosophy page states 「甘納豆は、純粋に豆と砂糖だけで作る菓子」. Still not dedicated — the 2F salon de thé menu is not itemised and the きな粉 item lists 澱粉 of unstated origin — so this is 'options', not 'high'.

name: 甘納豆かわむら (Amanatto Kawamura)
why: options — the record's vegan_detail hedges that 'some confections … may use dairy, eggs or honey', but the shop's own itemised 原材料 lists show zero animal ingredients across the whole retail range (beans, nuts, chestnut, sweet potato, citrus, olive, sugar, trehalose, reduced starch syrup). The 2F tea salon is separately branded and unlisted, which is why this is 'options' with an ask-at-the-salon caveat rather than 'full'.

name: カフェ 安江町ジャルダン (Cafe Yasuecho Jardin)
why: ask — the record calls the venue wheat-centric on the strength of a pancake it does not serve. The article publishes the full four-ingredient list of the 宝達くずミルクプリン (宝達葛, きび砂糖, 牛乳, 生クリーム, topped きな粉+黒蜜) — every one wheat-free — made to order in 20 minutes by a hands-on owner who tastes and approves each item. That is exactly an 'ask' situation, not a 'no'. Caveat for the human gate: scones are baked to order in the same small machiya kitchen, so airborne flour is a live risk and must stay in gf_detail.

name: フルーツむらはた 本店 (Fruit Murahata Honten)
why: The published menu is not wheat-free but it is not wheat-only either: 「◎まるごと夕張メロン 2,500円」「■フルーツごろごろジュレMIX 648円」「◎シャインマスカットソーダ 700円」「◎水蜜桃ヨーグルト」 are whole fruit, jelly, soda and yoghurt items that contain no wheat by construction, sold beside the ワッフル/タルト items. 'no' reads as 'nothing here is safe', which is wrong for a fruit parlour; 'ask' is honest because the company publishes no allergen policy anywhere on its site.

name: 甘味カフェ 茶ゆ (Kanmi Cafe Chayu)
why: options — the operator states in its own words that its signature item's wafer is gluten-free: 東山アイスもなか 「原材料に北陸産もち米のみを用いた最中種は自然な甘みと香ばしい風味が特徴のグルテンフリー」, and it publishes an アレルギー原材料 line for every gelato flavour, of which exactly one (金沢大野醤油＆焦がしキャラメル: 乳/卵/大豆/小麦) contains 小麦. 雪見アイスもなか is 最中種＋求肥＋粒餡 and the 2F menu is わらび餅・あんみつ・寒天・餡子 — all rice/agar/bean. Not 'high': どら焼き/チョコどら生地 and the deep-fried 金沢おでんカレーパン are made and handled in the same small shop, and no cross-contact protocol is published. But 'no' is wrong in the dangerous direction — it warns a celiac off a shop that labels its allergens and sells a rice-wafer signature.

name: 近江町食堂 (Omicho Shokudo)
why: gf_detail asserts 'no gluten-free menu, dedicated preparation, or allergen handling is documented', but the operator's own takeout page states 「※アレルギー対応が可能ですので、ご要望のある方はご相談ください。」 — allergy accommodation on request. That is documented allergen handling (scoped to pre-ordered オードブル platters), and the menu carries naturally GF anchors (刺身盛り合わせ, のどぐろ塩焼き, 金時草の酢の物). The wheat load is real (tempura, tonkatsu, うどん, 生麩田楽, one likely shared fryer), so this is 'ask and pre-arrange', not 'high' — but a flat 'no' both misstates the page and overstates the closure of the door.
